oidc_jwt.description: Reusing the same valid JWT can succeed multiple times because the JWT auth method documentation does not describe jti tracking or one-time JWT consumption.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay_same_token or stateless_jwt_no_jti as a vulnerability for Vault JWT auth unless a separate one-time mechanism was explicitly configured.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT leeway fields treat 0 as a nonzero default rather than strict zero leeway.
oidc_jwt.note: Boundary-time tokens may still validate when leeway is set to 0 because 0 selects the default buffer.

oidc_jwt.description: Token lookup-self display_name includes auth mount metadata as a prefix before the upstream identity value.
oidc_jwt.note: The oracle should ignore mount-derived prefixes when comparing granted identity to the sent identity.

oidc_jwt.description: Multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias name, which can cause them to share privileges through the same identity alias.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-user collisions may be by-design if alias cardinality is not unique; tests should distinguish platform behavior from misconfiguration.

oidc_jwt.description: An OIDC provider with empty allowed_client_ids allows no clients.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/provider Create or update a provider
oidc_jwt.note: Authorization failures in this state are expected and should not be treated as audience enforcement bugs.

oidc_jwt.description: Identity group policies apply only within the same namespace hierarchy by default.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing cross-namespace group policies is not necessarily an authorization bug under the default mode.

oidc_jwt.description: An OIDC client with no assignments allows no Vault entities to authenticate through the client; allow_all must be assigned to permit everyone.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/client Create or update a client
oidc_jwt.note: Authentication failure with no assignments is expected behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault's OIDC provider advertises request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false.
oidc_jwt.note: Unsigned request-object attacks are not applicable to this provider endpoint because request objects are unsupported.

oidc_jwt.constraint: JWT auth config requires exactly one trust source: configure_jwt_validation MUST set one and only one of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. Mixing them is invalid and omitting all of them leaves signature verification unconfigured.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer unless jwks_pairs is used. If bound_issuer is omitted, Vault will not compare the JWT iss claim, so issuer-substitution tests become meaningless.

JWT/OIDC role creation requires at least one bound value to be set. The fuzzer MUST configure at least one of bound_audiences, bound_subject, or bound_claims (or other documented bound values) or role setup is invalid.

For JWT roles carrying an aud claim, bound_audiences is required and must match at least one JWT aud value. For I5 audience tests, do not leave bound_audiences empty when the test token contains aud, or failures may reflect invalid setup rather than audience enforcement behavior.

bound_subject supports exact string match only; there is no companion bound_subject_type. Wildcards like '*' are treated literally. For I4 multi-identity tests, OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than setting a wildcard.

bound_audiences is exact list-membership matching only; there is no companion type parameter. Wildcards are not documented. For cross-identity or cross-provider tests that need multiple audiences to pass the same role, either supply the exact allowed audience values or omit the constraint where the test requires unconstrained audience behavior.

bound_claims matching semantics depend on bound_claims_type. Default bound_claims_type='string' means literal exact matching; only bound_claims_type='glob' interprets '*' as wildcard. For I4 multi-identity tests, do NOT set bound_claims to wildcard strings unless bound_claims_type is explicitly set to glob.

bound_claims accepts string, integer, boolean, or list-of-strings expected values. For I5 numeric coercion tests, set bound_claims_type to glob, not the default string, so numeric JWT claim values are coerced to strings rather than rejected outright by literal string matching.

user_claim must resolve to a string claim value. If the selected claim is absent, non-string, or incorrectly addressed without user_claim_json_pointer when using JSON Pointer syntax, login will fail for setup reasons rather than security reasons.

groups_claim must resolve to a list of strings. For I4/I5 type-confusion tests, a scalar string groups claim is by design invalid for group alias creation and should not be treated as a collision or escalation finding.

Numeric sentinel behavior for JWT leeways: clock_skew_leeway value 0 means use default 60 seconds, not strict zero; value -1 disables added leeway. expiration_leeway value 0 means use default 150 seconds; value -1 disables added leeway. not_before_leeway value 0 means use default 150 seconds; value -1 disables added leeway. Never assume 0 means strict enforcement.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests on JWT roles, include a control login using a valid token (for example exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}, iat={{now_epoch}}) alongside the attack token. Because Vault applies configurable leeways, an attack token near the boundary may still succeed by design.
OIDC authorization endpoint requires scope to include 'openid' and response_type='code'. Tests that omit openid or use unsupported response types are invalid setup, not security findings.

Vault OIDC provider documents nonce as optional but strongly encouraged. For OIDC SSO replay tests, the fuzzer MUST send a nonce in start_oidc_auth and verify the returned id_token contains the same nonce. Without a nonce, replay-oriented conclusions are not meaningful.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/provider Authorization endpoint and Token endpoint

oidc_jwt.constraint: PKCE is required for public clients and for any authorization code granted using PKCE. For confidential clients it is optional. Therefore, pkce_skip and pkce_not_required_public_client tests MUST distinguish client_type: missing code_verifier on a public client should fail by design, while confidential-client behavior depends on whether code_challenge was used.

redirect_uri matching is exact in both client registration and token exchange. The redirect_uri used at the token endpoint MUST exactly match the redirect_uri used when the authorization code was generated, and must be one of the client's configured redirect_uris.

Client assignments default to denying all Vault entities. To allow authentication through a Vault OIDC provider client, create_application MUST set assignments appropriately (for example the built-in allow_all) or attach an assignment containing the target entity/group IDs. Otherwise authorization failures are expected setup behavior.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/client Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC provider allowed_client_ids default to allowing no clients when empty. For provider-based OIDC tests, create_provider/configure the provider with allowed_client_ids including the target client_id or '*', otherwise all authorization attempts are denied by design.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/provider Create or update a provider

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC provider request_parameter_supported is false and request_uri_parameter_supported is false. Do NOT run oidc_request_object_alg_none tests against Vault's OIDC provider endpoints from this documentation; unsigned request objects are unsupported rather than improperly validated.

For OIDC audience-binding tests, use the client_id returned by the client configuration as the expected aud for issued id_tokens and as the client identifier at the token endpoint. Cross-client token acceptance tests must compare against exact client IDs because provider and client authorization are keyed by client_id.

Entity alias names are security-sensitive. Vault documentation warns that multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias and thereby share privileges. For I4 collision tests, treat alias reuse as a real risk surface and ensure each test identity uses a unique alias source unless intentionally probing collisions.

External identity groups used for JWT/OIDC group alias mapping should be populated via group aliases, not by manually setting member_entity_ids as if they were internal groups. Group alias mapping is the intended mechanism for external groups from claims.

Group policy application mode can broaden authorization across namespaces. If /sys/config/group-policy-application is set to 'any', group policies apply regardless of namespace hierarchy. Cross-namespace group-policy escalation tests must first read this global mode and treat 'any' as by-design broad application, not a broker bug.

Session-use budget: any token configured with num_uses or token_num_uses consumes a use on every authenticated API call, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. Minimum safe value is 2 if the sequence performs both self-lookup and secret-read after login; use 3 if an additional entity lookup is included.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/token lookup-self and token role fields shown in role reads

oidc_jwt.constraint: Numeric sentinel behavior for token use limits: token num_uses/token_num_uses value 0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. Never interpret 0 as 'single use' or 'disabled token'.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/token Create token and auth/jwt Read role sample

oidc_jwt.constraint: KV v2 paths are shape-sensitive. For verify_read_secret on a KV v2 mount, the read path MUST include /data/ (for example /v1/{engine}/data/{path}); using /v1/{engine}/{path} targets KV v1 and yields misleading 404s.

configure_jwt_validation MUST set exactly one of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. The JWT/OIDC auth config rejects combinations; do not attempt mixed trust-anchor setup in a single mount.
bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set. Do not build issuer-enforcement tests on a jwks_pairs configuration because the platform forbids that combination.
For JWT roles, create_auth_role requires at least one bound value to be set. A role with no bound constraints is invalid test setup.

bound_subject supports EXACT string match only. There is no companion type parameter for bound_subject. For I4 multi-identity tests, OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than setting '*' or other wildcard text, because wildcard characters are treated literally.

user_claim becomes the identity alias name and its claim value must be a string. For I4 tests, choose a string-valued claim such as sub or username; non-string claim values are invalid setup and will not create comparable aliases.

groups_claim must resolve to a list of strings. For I4/I5 group-mapping tests, do not send a scalar string when the role expects groups_claim; type-confusion outcomes may simply be rejected as invalid input rather than revealing alias-collision behavior.

bound_claims supports string, integer, boolean, or list-of-strings expected values, and bound_claims_type controls matching semantics. If bound_claims_type='string' (default), values are treated as literals and must match exactly. If bound_claims_type='glob', '*' is wildcard. For I4 multi-identity scenarios, OMIT exact-match bound_claims entries you need multiple identities to bypass; do not set them to '*' unless bound_claims_type is explicitly set to glob.

For I5 numeric coercion tests on bound_claims, set bound_claims_type to glob rather than the default string mode so non-string JWT claim values are coerced to strings for matching instead of being rejected outright. Then test integer bound value N against JWT float N+0.7 to detect silent coercion/truncation.

Numeric sentinel semantics: clock_skew_leeway uses 0 => default 60 seconds, -1 => disable extra leeway; expiration_leeway uses 0 => default 150 seconds, -1 => disable extra leeway; not_before_leeway uses 0 => default 150 seconds, -1 => disable extra leeway. Never assume 0 means strict zero tolerance.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a CONTROL login using a valid JWT alongside the attack JWT. Vault role leeway defaults (clock_skew_leeway 60s, expiration_leeway 150s, not_before_leeway 150s when set to 0) can make slightly stale or future tokens still succeed; without a control you cannot distinguish broken setup from intended leeway.

For I3 config-change tests, modify_role_config MUST tighten an existing role constraint or permission grant. Re-login after role changes is expected to use the NEW configuration by design; the valid oracle is that the same JWT accepted before is rejected after tightening, not that old behavior persists.

OIDC authorization requests to Vault's provider should include nonce even though the parameter is documented as optional. The docs strongly encourage nonce for replay mitigation; for I2/OIDC tests, omit nonce only when intentionally testing replay-related behavior.
Vault OIDC provider supports only response_type=code according to discovery metadata. Do not attempt implicit or hybrid-flow attack variants against this endpoint.

PKCE is REQUIRED for public clients and only optional for confidential clients. For pkce_skip and pkce_not_required_public_client tests, create_application with client_type='public' when you need mandatory PKCE behavior; a confidential client is allowed to omit PKCE by design.

redirect_uri matching is exact for Vault OIDC provider clients and the token endpoint requires the same redirect_uri used when the authorization code was generated. For redirect_uri_mismatch tests, vary only redirect_uri while keeping all other parameters constant.

Vault OIDC provider discovery advertises request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false. Do NOT run oidc_request_object_alg_none tests against this provider endpoint because request JWT objects are not supported here.

allowed_client_ids on an OIDC provider is authorization-critical: empty means no clients are allowed, '*' means all clients are allowed. For cross-client or cross-provider audience tests, do not accidentally set '*' unless broad client access is the intended setup.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/provider Create or update a provider

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC provider client assignments default to allowing NO Vault entities. To permit authentication through a client, create_application must include assignments, or use the built-in allow_all assignment when broad access is intended. Otherwise authorization failures are setup errors, not security findings.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/client Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC provider client_type and authentication method are immutable after creation. If a test needs to compare public vs confidential client behavior, create separate clients rather than trying to mutate one client mid-sequence.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/client Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: id_token_ttl should be less than the signing key's verification_ttl. If you rotate keys too aggressively or set verification_ttl too low, token validation failures after rotation may be by-design expiry of verification material rather than a trust-rotation bug.

Numeric sentinel semantics for Vault OIDC identity-token keys: allowed_client_ids empty => no roles/clients allowed, '*' => all allowed. For key rotation and audience-binding tests, do not treat empty as unrestricted.

Numeric sentinel semantics for KV v2: engine config max_versions=0 means keep 10 versions by default, not zero versions; delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic deletion timer. Do not assume zero disables storage or causes immediate deletion.
verify_read_secret on KV v2 MUST use the /data/ path segment. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} hits KV v1 semantics and yields misleading 404s.

KV v2 listing uses /metadata/ paths and requires list capability there even if reads/writes use /data/. If a test needs to enumerate keys, grant metadata-path list permissions explicitly; otherwise LIST failures are expected.

Session-use budget: any Vault token configured with num_uses or token_num_uses counts EVERY authenticated API call, including verify_granted_identity, verify_entity_details, and verify_read_secret. Minimum safe value is 2 if the sequence performs one verification call plus one protected-resource read; use 3+ if multiple verification calls occur first.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/token create, auth/jwt role read sample, userpass/saml tokenfields references

oidc_jwt.constraint: Numeric sentinel semantics for token use limits: token num_uses/token_num_uses value 0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. Do not treat 0 as one-time or disabled.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/token Create token and auth method tokenfields examples

oidc_jwt.constraint: verify_granted_identity via Vault OIDC provider /userinfo requires the access token from the token endpoint, not the id_token. session_token for OIDC flows must therefore map to access_token.

For I5 group-policy-escalation tests involving identity groups, be aware of the global group policy application mode. within_namespace_hierarchy is the default; any relaxes namespace restrictions and can broaden effective policies across namespaces by design.

configure_jwt_validation requires exactly one trust source: set ONE AND ONLY ONE of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. Do not send multiple trust sources in the same config or the setup is invalid.
bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set. Do not attempt issuer-binding tests with jwks_pairs because the API forbids that combination.

Every JWT/OIDC role must have at least one bound value set. The fuzzer MUST configure at least one of bound_audiences, bound_subject, or bound_claims (or other documented bound values) or role creation/update is invalid.
user_claim must resolve to a string claim value. If the selected claim is non-string, login will not produce a valid alias mapping. For I4 tests, choose a string-valued claim such as sub or username.

groups_claim must resolve to a list of strings. For I4/I5 group-mapping tests, sending a scalar string instead of an array is a type mismatch and should be treated as invalid setup, not a security finding.

bound_claims supports string, integer, boolean, or list-of-strings expected values. bound_claims_type='string' treats values as literals and requires exact matching; bound_claims_type='glob' interprets string values as globs with '*' wildcard. For I4 multi-identity scenarios, exact-match bound_claims entries must be omitted if multiple distinct values need to pass the same role.
Numeric sentinel semantics: clock_skew_leeway value 0 does NOT mean strict zero; it selects the default 60 seconds. Value -1 disables the extra leeway. Never assume 0 disables skew tolerance.
Numeric sentinel semantics: expiration_leeway value 0 does NOT mean strict zero; it selects the default 150 seconds. Value -1 disables the extra leeway. Never assume 0 disables expiration tolerance.
Numeric sentinel semantics: not_before_leeway value 0 does NOT mean strict zero; it selects the default 150 seconds. Value -1 disables the extra leeway. Never assume 0 disables nbf tolerance.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against JWT roles, include a CONTROL login using a valid token alongside the attack token. Because leeway defaults are nonzero (60s/150s), a near-expiry or near-future token may still be accepted by design.

OIDC auth_url uses Vault-generated state and nonce inside the returned auth_url. The callback requires both state and nonce query parameters. For I3/state-swap tests, preserve the exact state/nonce pair from the same auth_url response; mixing sessions is invalid setup.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt OIDC authorization URL request and callback

oidc_jwt.constraint: If auth mount config sets oidc_response_mode=form_post and Vault namespaces are in use, namespace_in_state should be false. Otherwise redirect handling can break for OIDC flows and produce false negatives unrelated to security.
OIDC response type id_token may only be used when oidc_response_mode is form_post. Do not configure id_token response type in other modes when testing OIDC flow behavior.
For OIDC provider authorization requests, the openid scope is required. Missing openid is invalid setup, not a security failure.

For Vault OIDC provider clients, redirect_uri must exactly match one of the configured redirect_uris on the client, and the token endpoint redirect_uri must match the one used when the code was issued. For redirect_uri mismatch tests, assert rejection by status/result rather than identity differences.

Public OIDC clients must use PKCE: code_challenge is required at authorize time and code_verifier is required at token time. Confidential clients may omit PKCE. Do not treat PKCE enforcement for public clients as optional on this platform.

Vault's OIDC provider metadata explicitly reports request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false. Do NOT run oidc_request_object_alg_none tests against this provider endpoint because request JWTs are unsupported and any rejection is by design.

For OIDC SSO validation tests on Vault as relying party, the callback requires nonce and state from the same auth_url flow, and the provider token response example includes nonce in the ID token. A valid replay test must preserve a control flow with matching nonce; otherwise callback failure may just reflect broken flow binding.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt OIDC authorization URL request and callback; identity/oidc/provider token example

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC provider allowed_client_ids semantics: empty allowed_client_ids means NO clients are allowed; '*' means all clients are allowed. Do not use an empty list when you intend unrestricted access.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/provider Create or update a provider

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC client assignments semantics: by default, no Vault entities are allowed to authenticate through a client. To allow all entities, use the built-in allow_all assignment. If assignments are omitted, login failures are expected and not evidence of a bug.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/client Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC client_type is immutable after creation, and key is also immutable after creation. For I3 config-change tests involving client_type or signing key, create a new client instead of attempting in-place mutation.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/client Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC client TTL parameters are security-relevant durations: id_token_ttl and access_token_ttl default to 24h. Use short explicit TTLs for freshness tests; otherwise long-lived tokens may remain valid by design.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/client Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC named key verification_ttl controls how long old public keys remain available after rotation. During key-rotation tests, acceptance of tokens signed by an old key may persist until verification_ttl expires if clients validate against retained public keys. Distinguish trust-anchor rotation on JWT auth mounts from OIDC provider key publication retention.

Numeric sentinel semantics: KV v2 engine max_versions value 0 does NOT mean keep zero versions; it means use the default retention of 10 versions. delete_version_after value '0s' means no automatic deletion timer. Never assume 0 disables storage or causes immediate deletion.
verify_read_secret on KV v2 MUST use the /data/ path segment. Using /{mount}/{path} without /data/ hits the wrong API shape and causes false 404/permission errors.
KV v2 list operations require policy on the /metadata/ path even if reads/writes use /data/. If the fuzzer seeds or verifies list behavior, grant list capability on /metadata/ explicitly.

Session-use budget: token num_uses counts every API call made with that token, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. Minimum safe value is 2 if the sequence performs both a verification call and a protected-resource read; use 3+ if additional self-lookups occur.

External identity groups should be populated via group aliases from auth methods, not by manually setting member_entity_ids for the purpose of JWT/OIDC external group mapping. Manual membership can change authorization semantics and invalidate group-claim escalation tests.

Group policy application mode can be globally set to 'within_namespace_hierarchy' or 'any'. For I5 group-policy-escalation tests, record the current mode first: in 'any' mode, cross-namespace group policies applying broadly is by configuration, not necessarily a bug.
